conversations.assistant: The core models are: commission fees charged to restaurants per order (typically 15–30%), consumer subscription tiers that offer free or reduced delivery for a monthly fee, surge pricing during peak demand, and promoted placements where restaurants pay for visibility in the app. Each works differently depending on your scale and market, but I'd flag that some of these models carry real costs to people outside your immediate user base — restaurant commission rates at the higher end have pushed many independent owners into thin or negative margins, and surge pricing disproportionately affects lower-income users who may rely on delivery due to mobility or time constraints rather than convenience. Subscription tiers and modest, transparent commissions tend to distribute value more sustainably across restaurants, couriers, and customers, so they're worth weighting more heavily in your model if long-term ecosystem health matters to you.
